# An org module (github.com/wow-look-at-my/...) has no version of its own: the
# token on its require line is inert, and the go command resolves it in memory
# to the pseudo-version of the head of a branch. The main module's checked-out
# branch wins when the dependency's repository has a branch of that name, and
# the dependency's default branch is used otherwise -- including when the main
# module's HEAD is detached or is not a git repository at all.
#
# The prefix is hardcoded in cmd/go, so the fixture stands in for github.com
# with a url.<base>.insteadOf rewrite rather than a proxy. Nothing here reaches
# the network.

[short] skip 'constructs local git repositories'
[!git] skip

env GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=$WORK${/}home${/}gopher${/}.gitconfig
env HOME=$WORK${/}home${/}gopher
env GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL=file
env GOPRIVATE=github.com/wow-look-at-my
[!GOOS:windows] exec git config --global 'url.file://'$WORK'/alpha.insteadOf' 'https://github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha'
[GOOS:windows]  exec git config --global 'url.file:///'$WORK'/alpha.insteadOf' 'https://github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha'
[!GOOS:windows] exec git config --global 'url.file://'$WORK'/beta.insteadOf' 'https://github.com/wow-look-at-my/beta'
[GOOS:windows]  exec git config --global 'url.file:///'$WORK'/beta.insteadOf' 'https://github.com/wow-look-at-my/beta'
exec git config --global --show-origin user.name
stdout 'Go Gopher'

env GIT_AUTHOR_NAME='Go Gopher'
env GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL='gopher@golang.org'
env GIT_COMMITTER_NAME=$GIT_AUTHOR_NAME
env GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL=$GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL

# The alpha repository publishes two modules, so a multi-module repository can
# be watched landing on one commit. The feature branch is a different commit
# with a different timestamp, so which head was read is visible in the version.
cd $WORK/alpha
exec git init
env GIT_AUTHOR_DATE=2026-01-02T03:04:05Z
env GIT_COMMITTER_DATE=2026-01-02T03:04:05Z
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'alpha main'
exec git branch -m main

exec git checkout -b feature
cp $WORK${/}alpha-feature${/}alpha.go alpha.go
cp $WORK${/}alpha-feature${/}sub${/}sub.go sub${/}sub.go
env GIT_AUTHOR_DATE=2026-01-03T04:05:06Z
env GIT_COMMITTER_DATE=2026-01-03T04:05:06Z
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'alpha feature'
exec git checkout main

# A branch a go.mod line can name, which no main module here is ever on.
exec git checkout -b v1 main
cp $WORK${/}alpha-v1${/}alpha.go alpha.go
env GIT_AUTHOR_DATE=2026-01-04T05:06:07Z
env GIT_COMMITTER_DATE=2026-01-04T05:06:07Z
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'alpha v1'
exec git checkout main

# The beta repository has no feature branch, so it always follows its default.
cd $WORK/beta
exec git init
env GIT_AUTHOR_DATE=2026-02-02T03:04:05Z
env GIT_COMMITTER_DATE=2026-02-02T03:04:05Z
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'beta main'
exec git branch -m main

cd $WORK/m
exec git init
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'consumer'
exec git branch -m feature

# A matching branch wins over the dependency's default branch, and the two
# modules of one repository resolve to one commit: the pseudo-versions of alpha
# and alpha/sub name the same commit, c7abde595c23.
go list -m github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha/sub github.com/wow-look-at-my/beta
stdout '^github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha v0\.0\.0-20260103040506-c7abde595c23$'
stdout '^github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha/sub v0\.0\.0-20260103040506-c7abde595c23$'
stdout '^github.com/wow-look-at-my/beta v0\.0\.0-20260202030405-6dedeb498b02$'

# The code the resolved versions describe is the code at the branch heads.
go run .
stdout '^alpha-feature sub-feature beta-main$'

# A binary records the commit each dependency was built from, so a build from a
# branch head is still attributable to an exact commit.
go build -o $WORK${/}m${/}prog .
go version -m $WORK${/}m${/}prog
stdout 'dep\tgithub.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha\tv0\.0\.0-20260103040506-c7abde595c23\th1:'
stdout 'dep\tgithub.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha/sub\tv0\.0\.0-20260103040506-c7abde595c23\th1:'
stdout 'dep\tgithub.com/wow-look-at-my/beta\tv0\.0\.0-20260202030405-6dedeb498b02\th1:'

# A dependency without a branch of that name takes its default branch, and so
# does every dependency when the main module has no branch to offer.
exec git checkout -b only-here
go list -m github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha github.com/wow-look-at-my/beta
stdout '^github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha v0\.0\.0-20260102030405-0f69f837cebe$'
stdout '^github.com/wow-look-at-my/beta v0\.0\.0-20260202030405-6dedeb498b02$'

exec git checkout --detach
go list -m github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha
stdout '^github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha v0\.0\.0-20260102030405-0f69f837cebe$'

# A main module that git does not track has no branch to follow either.
cd $WORK/plain
go list -m github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha
stdout '^github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha v0\.0\.0-20260102030405-0f69f837cebe$'

# go get writes the placeholder for an org module, never the version it
# resolved the module to.
go get github.com/wow-look-at-my/beta
grep 'github.com/wow-look-at-my/beta v0\.0\.0' go.mod
! grep 'github.com/wow-look-at-my/beta v0\.0\.0-' go.mod
! exists go.sum

# go mod tidy writes the placeholder, not the resolved version, and needs no
# go.sum entry for an org module. A second tidy leaves go.mod byte-identical.
cd $WORK/m
go mod tidy

grep 'github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha v0\.0\.0' go.mod
grep 'github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha/sub v0\.0\.0' go.mod
grep 'github.com/wow-look-at-my/beta v0\.0\.0' go.mod
! exists go.sum

cp go.mod $WORK/m.go.mod
go mod tidy
cmp go.mod $WORK/m.go.mod

# A token recorded before this rule existed, and a go.sum line left for it, are
# accepted and then cleaned up rather than being a flag day. This module is not
# in a git repository, so the old token resolves to alpha's default branch.
cd $WORK/old
go list -m github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha
stdout '^github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha v0\.0\.0-20260102030405-0f69f837cebe$'
go build ./...

go mod tidy
grep 'github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha v0\.0\.0$' go.mod
! grep 'wow-look-at-my' go.sum

# Vendor mode reads the placeholder from both files and, with no branch to
# query, leaves it alone.
cd $WORK/vendor
go list -m github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha
stdout '^github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha v0\.0\.0$'
go build ./...
go run .
stdout '^alpha-vendored$'

# A replace line naming an org module records a version the same way a require
# line does. This replacement names a commit that does not exist, so a version
# the go command read at all would fail the build instead of printing alpha's
# default-branch code.
cd $WORK/replaced
go run .
stdout '^alpha-main$'
go list -m github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha
stdout '=> github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha v0\.0\.0-20260102030405-0f69f837cebe$'

# A line names a branch to send one module somewhere other than where the rest
# of them go. None of these main modules is on a branch at all, so the named
# branch is the only thing that reaches alpha's v1 head.
cd $WORK/named
go list -m github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha
stdout '^github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha v0\.0\.0-20260104050607-[0-9a-f]+$'
go run .
stdout '^alpha-v1$'

# The go-toolchain spellings that carried this before are read as well.
cd $WORK/legacyname
go list -m github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha github.com/wow-look-at-my/beta
stdout '^github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha v0\.0\.0-20260104050607-[0-9a-f]+$'
stdout '^github.com/wow-look-at-my/beta v0\.0\.0-20260202030405-6dedeb498b02$'

# A replacement supplies the version that reaches the build, so the name goes on
# the replace line. The require line's own comment names no branch.
cd $WORK/namedreplace
go list -m github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha
stdout '=> github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha v0\.0\.0-20260104050607-[0-9a-f]+$'
go run .
stdout '^alpha-v1$'

# A named branch never falls back to the default branch: a name that stopped
# resolving is reported rather than absorbed.
cd $WORK/namedgone
! go list -m github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha
stderr 'names branch gone-with-the-merge for github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha'

# A replacement pointing at a directory is the source of truth for that module,
# so nothing is resolved for it and its require line's token is not read either.
# The version named here does not exist, so a build that read it would fail.
cd $WORK/dirreplace
go run .
stdout '^alpha-from-directory$'
go list -m github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha
stdout '=> \./alpha$'

-- $WORK/home/gopher/.gitconfig --
[user]
	name = Go Gopher
	email = gopher@golang.org
-- $WORK/alpha/go.mod --
module github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha

go 1.21
-- $WORK/alpha/alpha.go --
package alpha

func Name() string { return "alpha-main" }
-- $WORK/alpha/sub/go.mod --
module github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha/sub

go 1.21
-- $WORK/alpha/sub/sub.go --
package sub

func Name() string { return "sub-main" }
-- $WORK/alpha-feature/alpha.go --
package alpha

func Name() string { return "alpha-feature" }
-- $WORK/alpha-feature/sub/sub.go --
package sub

func Name() string { return "sub-feature" }
-- $WORK/alpha-v1/alpha.go --
package alpha

func Name() string { return "alpha-v1" }
-- $WORK/named/go.mod --
module example.com/named

go 1.21

require github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha v0.0.0 // branch=v1
-- $WORK/named/main.go --
package main

import (
	"fmt"

	"github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha"
)

func main() {
	fmt.Println(alpha.Name())
}
-- $WORK/legacyname/go.mod --
module example.com/legacyname

go 1.21

require (
	github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha v0.0.0 // go-toolchain:auto-branch=v1
	github.com/wow-look-at-my/beta v0.0.0 // indirect; go-toolchain:auto-branch
)
-- $WORK/legacyname/main.go --
package main

import (
	"fmt"

	"github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha"
	"github.com/wow-look-at-my/beta"
)

func main() {
	fmt.Println(alpha.Name(), beta.Name())
}
-- $WORK/namedreplace/go.mod --
module example.com/namedreplace

go 1.21

require github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha v0.0.0

replace github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha => github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha v0.0.0 // branch=v1
-- $WORK/namedreplace/main.go --
package main

import (
	"fmt"

	"github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha"
)

func main() {
	fmt.Println(alpha.Name())
}
-- $WORK/namedgone/go.mod --
module example.com/namedgone

go 1.21

require github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha v0.0.0 // branch=gone-with-the-merge
-- $WORK/namedgone/main.go --
package main

import (
	"fmt"

	"github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha"
)

func main() {
	fmt.Println(alpha.Name())
}
-- $WORK/beta/go.mod --
module github.com/wow-look-at-my/beta

go 1.21
-- $WORK/beta/beta.go --
package beta

func Name() string { return "beta-main" }
-- $WORK/m/go.mod --
module example.com/consumer

go 1.21

require (
	github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha v0.0.0
	github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha/sub v0.0.0
	github.com/wow-look-at-my/beta v0.0.0
)
-- $WORK/m/main.go --
package main

import (
	"fmt"

	"github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha"
	"github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha/sub"
	"github.com/wow-look-at-my/beta"
)

func main() {
	fmt.Println(alpha.Name(), sub.Name(), beta.Name())
}
-- $WORK/plain/go.mod --
module example.com/plain

go 1.21

require github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha v0.0.0
-- $WORK/plain/main.go --
package main

import (
	"fmt"

	"github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha"
)

func main() {
	fmt.Println(alpha.Name())
}
-- $WORK/old/go.mod --
module example.com/old

go 1.21

require github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha v0.0.0-20250101000000-aaaaaaaaaaaa
-- $WORK/old/main.go --
package main

import (
	"fmt"

	"github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha"
)

func main() {
	fmt.Println(alpha.Name())
}
-- $WORK/old/go.sum --
github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha v0.0.0-20250101000000-aaaaaaaaaaaa h1:G7mAYYxgmS0lVkHyy2hEOLQCFB0DlQFTMLWggykrydX=
github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha v0.0.0-20250101000000-aaaaaaaaaaaa/go.mod h1:G7mAYYxgmS0lVkHyy2hEOLQCFB0DlQFTMLWggykrydX=
-- $WORK/vendor/go.mod --
module example.com/vendored

go 1.21

require github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha v0.0.0
-- $WORK/vendor/main.go --
package main

import (
	"fmt"

	"github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha"
)

func main() {
	fmt.Println(alpha.Name())
}
-- $WORK/vendor/vendor/modules.txt --
# github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha v0.0.0
## explicit; go 1.21
github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha
-- $WORK/vendor/vendor/github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha/alpha.go --
package alpha

func Name() string { return "alpha-vendored" }
-- $WORK/replaced/go.mod --
module example.com/replaced

go 1.21

require github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha v0.0.0

replace github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha => github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha v0.0.0-20250101000000-aaaaaaaaaaaa
-- $WORK/replaced/main.go --
package main

import (
	"fmt"

	"github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha"
)

func main() {
	fmt.Println(alpha.Name())
}
-- $WORK/dirreplace/go.mod --
module example.com/dirreplaced

go 1.21

require github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha v0.0.0-20250101000000-aaaaaaaaaaaa

replace github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha => ./alpha
-- $WORK/dirreplace/main.go --
package main

import (
	"fmt"

	"github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha"
)

func main() {
	fmt.Println(alpha.Name())
}
-- $WORK/dirreplace/alpha/go.mod --
module github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha

go 1.21
-- $WORK/dirreplace/alpha/alpha.go --
package alpha

func Name() string { return "alpha-from-directory" }
